subject: Biochemistry
vignette: A 5-month-old boy is evaluated for developmental delay and hypotonia. He was born at term, has had several episodes of seizures, and cannot hold his head up. His hair is sparse, depigmented, and brittle, with a twisted, kinky appearance, and his cheeks are unusually full. Serum copper and ceruloplasmin are low. Imaging shows tortuous, dilated cerebral vessels. The boy's maternal uncle died in infancy with a similar illness.
question: Impaired activity of which of the following enzymes best explains the connective tissue and vascular abnormalities in this patient?
explanation_correct: Menkes disease is an X-linked recessive disorder caused by defective ATP7A, which normally mediates intestinal copper absorption and copper transfer into the trans-Golgi. Copper deficiency impairs lysyl oxidase, a copper-dependent enzyme that cross-links collagen and elastin, so hair becomes brittle and kinky and arteries are weakened, predisposing to cerebral aneurysms; loss of tyrosinase, another copper enzyme, explains depigmented hair and of cytochrome c oxidase the hypotonia and seizures.

explanation_incorrect.A: Prolyl hydroxylase requires vitamin C and hydroxylates proline in collagen; its deficiency causes scurvy, not kinky hair with arterial tortuosity.
explanation_incorrect.B: Lysyl hydroxylase is also a vitamin C-dependent collagen-modifying enzyme and is not a copper enzyme, so it is not the mechanism of Menkes disease.
explanation_incorrect.C: Copper-containing superoxide dismutase 1 protects against oxidative stress, and its loss does not account for defective collagen and elastin cross-linking.
explanation_incorrect.E: Tyrosinase is a copper-dependent enzyme, but its loss explains the depigmented hair rather than the connective tissue and vascular fragility.

educationalObjective: Menkes disease impairs copper delivery to copper-dependent enzymes, and reduced lysyl oxidase activity causes defective collagen and elastin cross-linking with kinky hair and arterial weakness.
